John Booth confirmed his fitness with an outstanding 1500m win and young Jamie Webb travelled all the way from the other side of Essex to chip in with full points in the vault.

…you believe it - he was the only one who managed to compete without getting a soaking), Aham Amadi, Neil Hammersley and Jamie Webb, we managed to avoid last place but dropped three more places to 22nd overall.…

Another athlete who could be classed "a team manager's dream," Jamie Webb lives out Essex way but travels to Tooting or Battersea for mid-week Rosenheim meets and anywhere you care to name for a Southern or National Junior League.

…ike Phil Carstairs who had ridden 30 miles on his bike to make sure that he could line up for the 3k, the ever-reliable Jamie Webb never missing an opportunity to take in another 'vaulting competition and reserves queuing up to fill in, we have a great mid-week outfit.…

A great double win came from high jumpers Mark Arend and James Ganio, and Jamie Webb again did the business in the pole vault but once more the team had a makeshift look about it as we had to get people competing 'just for the point'; when did you last see Guy Sagar and Bob Bridges forming our 800m line-up?

Our other winner was Jamie Webb - but he was lucky. Not that he had any trouble clearing 3.70m in the pole vault, it's just that he competed in a non-club vest (with the judge's permission) and then had the meeting organiser querying his lack of 'claret and gold'.

Jamie Webb had no such problems, this being his side of the country, but he was also on a 'high'. Having already set a pb in the 'vault, he had the bar set at 4 metres and was delighted with yet another clearance.

Another young man at the top of his form late in the season was Jamie Webb, soaring over a pole vault bar set at 4.15m for a fine pb. Much more improvement and the Southern League Team will be losing him to the British League.

The weather was nasty for pole vaulting but Jamie Webb and Susie Drummie kept the Belgrave colours flying high and at least had the right equipment to get to their cars should the water level in the car park rise any higher.
Our young vaulters appreciated having Jamie Webb on hand to advise them and they both did well to win, having some four years ahead of them in this competition.

Said Chettati equalled his best ever in the 5k as did Jamie Webb in the 'vault, both in spite of the miserable weather. Well, we're 21st in the league now, with some of the top clubs to meet next time.

Long jumpers Pete Mercer and Chido Edozie collected our only max on the field although the vaulters came close with Jamie Webb always over 4 metres now and Terry Lawton setting new personal best figures and earning himself a representative berth for Surrey in a vets inter-county match.
The pole vault proved to be a hot competition but when Jamie Webb damaged his ankle by landing in the box we had more to worry about than winning an extra point or two.

Incessant rain and a strong wind put paid to the pole vault competition before it began but Jamie Webb, rather than go all that way for nothing, turned out in the 'B' 400 hurdles and surprised himself by picking up a second place.

In 1996 Jamie Webb raised his best 'vault another 15cm to 4.40m and broke into the British League team for the first time. Left: Kevin Brown finished the season as Belgrave's most prolific points scorer in British Athletic League matches.

Things got a little harder as the season progressed and we lost sprinter Marlon Dickson, vaulter Jamie Webb and 400 flat and hurdles man Jon Squirrell to the British League team but to be honest, this just gave some of the younger men a chance to show their mettle - and they grasped the chance.
